newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen steady, waiting for Wednesday data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen steady, waiting for Wednesday data.

text.p: The benchmark three-month March euroyen futures contract ended extremely thin Tuesday trade unchanged, with many operators sidelined ahead of Wednesday's release of key Japanese production data, traders said.

Although some light sales did emerge after comments from a former Ministry of Finance (MOF) official bruised JGB futures, the impact was strictly limited, they added. The key March contract settled at 99.11, steady on Monday's figure.
March drifted narrowly from 99.09 to 99.12 and while tone remained firm overall, a lack of fresh buying factors amid the general wait-and-see mood kept most in the market from moving.
"Last week's muted Bank of Japan (BOJ) economic outlook and recent indicators are keeping sentiment firm, but without anything fresh to move on rises are difficult," a trader said.

Makoto Utsumi, former MOF vice-minister for international affairs, told Reuters Financial Television that JGBs are trading at "bubble" levels and prices are likely to see a downward correction due to increased Japanese economic activity.

This sent JGBs temporarily lower, pushing euroyen futures down as well. But the impact was brief, with a bout of speculative buying pushing the key March euroyen contract to its day's high of 99.12 shortly after.

The market is fixated on Wednesday's release of June Japanese industrial production figures and predictions for July and August. An average of economists' forecasts showed Japan's industrial output is expected to have fallen 2.8 percent in June from the previous month after a large increase in May. Forecasts ranged from a fall of 1.2 percent to a fall of 4.0 percent. The data will be announced at 0430 GMT Wednesday.

Euroyen traders said that if there is a greater fall than expected in the June figures, euroyen futures are likely to see some healthy buying, perhaps trying the key 99.14 level and then 99.20. But others said this is unlikely to have much impact and that predictions for July and August will carry much Overnight call money was trading at 0.48 percent and 0.49 percent in the afternoon, and traders said the weighted average was likely to remain unchanged at 0.48 percent.
But in light of the BOJ's morning operation, rates were surprisingly strong, they added.

The central bank injected 200 billion yen into the money market in the face of a 110 billion yen surplus, keeping the market in surplus by an overall 300 billion yen for the fifth consecutive trading day.

In the longer end of the market, around 10 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.65 percent, unchanged from Monday. Around 20 billion yen of two-month CDs were issued at 0.59 percent, unchanged from July 16, the last time two-month CDs were issued.
